assessment.shape: The source provides a robust fusiform body, conical snout, large first dorsal fin, small second dorsal/anal fins, five gill openings and crescent caudal fin. Its tooth rows, serrations, jaw tissue and exact fin/body ratios remain simplified; the model is not fitted to the photographed individual.
assessment.surface: Material conversion restored the source countershading, scars and fine normal detail. The white ventral boundary is preserved across swimming. Some scars and fine textures are conspicuous artistic choices, and denticle microanatomy is unresolved.
assessment.motion: The retained creator skeleton and Swimming clip use lateral propulsion. Two substantially different phases were viewed from side/front/top. Mouth and body mechanics are not calibrated; archived Circling/Biting clips were not relabelled as complete biological behaviors.
changes: Converted the legacy source material to supported PBR while preserving mesh positions, UVs, joints, weights and three source clip channel sets.
Mapped only the creator Swimming clip to the supported motion control.
Kept the same body airborne above the aquatic specimen desk in Observe and Swim.
Added authentic Terry Goss photograph and Smithsonian STRI species-account context.
remaining: Source clip timing and fin flexibility have not been compared to a fitted measured sequence.
Teeth, dermal denticles, ventilation and prey-contact mechanics remain incomplete.
No claim of measured speed, force, energetics or validated hunting.

photograph.description: An authentic white-shark photograph at Isla Guadalupe, Mexico, August 2006. The source gives an estimated individual length; the model is not fitted to that estimate.
photograph.identityScope: Photographer/Commons species association and visibly compatible diagnostic outline; no independent specimen determination or measured model fit.
photograph.changes: Faithful resize and JPEG encoding; no generated content, anatomical edits or color replacement.

model.title: Animated Swimming Great White Shark Loop
model.author: LasquetiSpice (https://sketchfab.com/LasquetiSpice)
model.delivery: Bundled GLB; one local viewer and same retained textured mesh through supported actions
model.biology: Artist interpretation; species identity, surface and unmeasured motion reviewed against cited sources but not independently validated.
model.changes: The original creator Swimming clip drives the retained skeleton, skin weights and textures. It uses lateral body/tail movement. Creator Circling and Biting clips are archived but are not exposed as scientifically validated hunting or escape behaviors; no prey capture or fluid calculation is implemented. The obsolete specular/glossiness material extension was converted to supported glTF PBR materials. Source positions, UVs, weights, joints and clip channels were retained; source and delivered checksums differ and are separately recorded.
